title: Integration of transcriptomics and metabolomics reveals the cytotoxic mechanisms of microplastics in BEAS-2B cells
content:
Abstract
Polyethylene (PE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) are the most common microplastics (MPs) in daily life. We used transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to investigate the toxic mechanisms of five MPs on BEAS-2B cells. Cells were exposed to different concentrations (0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, and 1,000 μg/ml) of five MPs. The CCK8 results showed significant differences at 800 μg/ml. Transcriptomics analysis revealed 1,412, 162, 530, 126, and 4,940 DEGs in PET, PE, PVC, PP, and PS groups, mainly involved in PI3K-Akt, MAPK signaling pathways. The mutual DEG was ANKLE1. Metabolomics analysis identified 2,869, 4,415, 3,768, 2088 and 4,264 DEMs in five groups, primarily involved in pyruvate, purine metabolism. Multi-omics analysis these microplastics mainly interfered with lipid and nucleotide metabolism pathways, which may increase the risk of cell apoptosis. This study analyzed the toxicity effects of five microplastics, emphasizing potential human health risks.
